name: Impasto
summary: A moving oil painting made of thick palette-knife strokes raked by low light so every ridge shows: value-planned, readable at thumbnail size, colour laid in planes of slightly broken paint, titles laid in with the knife, and colour itself as the event.
suits: colour returns stories (recovery, relaunch, a town waking)

palette.use: cobalt: the top of an after-rain sky, the default ground
titanium cream: titles laid in with the knife, crisp small text (proposed)
burnt umber: calm dark planes behind diagrams (the source's 'night kitchen' umber, proposed hex)
cadmium red: the subject's colour, the brightest and purest, the first colour back
pure cobalt: blue light, the second subject colour
the low sky, the sun, sunlight
the deep ultramarine end-card ground (proposed hex)
dark paint for type on light planes, cast ridges (proposed)

type.emphasis: a word laid in a pure subject colour

motion.enter: laid in stroke by stroke by the knife (a sweep), or re-painted from grey to colour by a reveal wave
motion.exit: painted over, scraped, or washed by the weather

banned: a swirl filter or strokes boiling everywhere: static paint never moves
a brush texture over flat vector art, or a painterly photo filter: strokes are designed
dissolves (two layers of knife ridges turn to mud)
film grain (it eats the knife edges)
pixel-blended gradients: a gradient is stroke-to-stroke steps
strokes crossing from one shape into another: silhouettes stay crisp
a painted rectangle for a reflection, or plain rectangles as figures
the camera leaving the painted plate
copying a painter's or film's images, compositions or characters
